definition: Impartial means not favoring one side over another.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word impartial. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know impartial should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The dispute was settled by an impartial mediator who had no ties to either family.
A neutral observer simply takes no side, while an impartial judge actively weighs both sides with equal fairness.
An impartial referee favors no one today, while an incorruptible one could never be swayed by any bribe or pressure.

Unbiased means free from personal preference or slant, and it describes someone actually weighing or reporting something — a juror, a referee, a news story. Impartial is its close partner for decision-makers who treat both sides with equal fairness. You can only be unbiased about a judgment you are actually making; impartial likewise presumes you are judging.

Objective means based on facts rather than feelings — an objective review lets the evidence decide. Impartial is about sides rather than sources: an impartial judge favors neither party, whatever the evidence says. A critic can be objective about a lone film with no contest in sight, while impartiality matters exactly when two sides face off.

When the regional science fair grew to three hundred entries, the organizers rewrote the rules for judging.
Every judge now scores projects from a school other than their own, and the students' names are replaced with numbers before the scorecards go out.
The aim is an impartial panel: judges who favor neither the polished private academies nor the scrappy public schools, and who give each entry the same twenty minutes.
One veteran judge admits the old system tugged at her loyalties, since her niece competed for years.
Under the new rules she says the tug is gone; whichever school a project comes from, it gets the same questions, the same rubric, and the same chance.
